items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: He said, 'well my name is Jerry Jerome,' he says, 'you know, when I first met you you came -- I was going to the University of Alabama studying medicine, and you came there with Earl Hines'

ctx.x: Of course that was really no (unintelligible) as popular as he was in the many things he was. He probably was ace at the stockmarkets and you know, but any way. I always admired Toots. But any way we were recording, so I felt this man looking at me on my left, and he's looking and he finally said, 'Bud, you don't remember me, do you?' And I said 'tell you the truth, I really can't call you a name, you know, it's (unintelligible). He said, 'well my name is Jerry Jerome,' he says, 'you know, when I first met you…

I went on to say that this was my first record with Jerome Jones. So when we're in the White Rose, he came in and he says Bud Johnson. I said, hey, J., what do you know, baby. Oh, fine, have a drink. I said, okay, don't care if I do. So we're drinking and he said something, meet my manager,

He introduced me to his manager, I forget his name. So he says what are you doing, I said, well I'm working around the corner on the street. He said, are you still writing those beautiful arrangements. I said, well I'm still writing, Jerry. He says, well let me tell you, I'm now a conductor for NBC, and he says, I certainly would like for you to write some music for me. I said, well, it would be a pleasure, he says okay meet me up to NBC tomorrow at 9:30 in the morning and we'll take you and see what we can do.…
